title: Nearby Friends
oneLine: Treat location as expiring soft state, maintain WebSocket connections, and fan location updates only to authorized online friends through partitioned pub/sub.
opening: Unlike a business proximity index, friend locations are highly dynamic and privacy-sensitive. Mobile clients periodically send coarse location updates over a persistent connection or API. A location service validates consent and precision, stores the latest location with a short TTL, and publishes an update keyed by user. Each connected user’s gateway or nearby service subscribes only to authorized online friends, computes exact distance, and pushes enter/leave/update events. Connection and topic ownership are partitioned by user ID, with service discovery mapping users to gateways and pub/sub shards. The system is eventually consistent by design; stale locations expire automatically. I would make opt-in, invisible mode, block lists, precision reduction, audit, and abuse controls first-class rather than treating location as ordinary profile data.
ask: Friends only, mutual friends, or any nearby users?
What distance, accuracy, update frequency, and battery budget?
What privacy modes and block/visibility rules apply?
Do we need history, or only current expiring location?
scale: Model location updates separately from socket count: 100M active users updating every 30 seconds is about 3.3M updates/s.
Fanout = update rate × online authorized friends; filter subscriptions aggressively rather than broadcasting spatially to everyone.
Location TTL should exceed a few missed updates but be short enough that offline users disappear safely.

decisions.default: User-topic pub/sub to online authorized friends.
decisions.why: A typical user has a bounded friend set; it avoids publishing every location into public spatial cells.
decisions.switch: For ‘people nearby’ discovery, use geohash/S2 cell topics with strict privacy and aggregation.

decisions.default: Redis-like expiring latest state; append history only if explicitly required.
decisions.why: Current location is soft state and automatic expiry prevents indefinite stale visibility.
decisions.switch: Durable encrypted history requires a separate retention/legal design.

decisions.default: Adaptive client cadence based on movement, app state, and battery.
decisions.why: Fixed high-frequency GPS updates waste battery and backend capacity.
decisions.switch: Higher frequency for explicit live-sharing sessions with time-limited consent.

decisions.default: Compute exact distance after authorization, with coarse cells only for candidate reduction if needed.
decisions.why: Privacy filtering must precede disclosure and cell membership is approximate.
decisions.switch: Do calculations on device for stronger privacy where product flow permits.

deepDives.title: Subscription management
points: On login, fetch authorized online-friend set and subscribe in batches.
Process follow/block/privacy changes as events that add/remove subscriptions immediately.
For whale users, cap subscriptions and use pull or hierarchical fanout.

deepDives.title: Gateway scaling
points: Shard users by consistent hashing; keep device registry with TTL and topology epoch.
Drain gateways by stopping new connections and forcing jittered reconnect.
Delivery is best effort; reconnect fetches current location snapshot rather than replaying every movement.

deepDives.title: Privacy engineering
points: Reduce coordinate precision and show distance bands rather than raw coordinates.
Prevent background location collection outside active consent.
Rate-limit lookups and detect stalking/scraping patterns.

failures.risk: User goes offline but remains visible
failures.response: Short TTL, heartbeat expiry, and client-side ‘last updated’ display/threshold.
Authorize again before delivery, version policies, remove subscriptions immediately, and reject stale policy epochs.
Rebuild subscriptions from friend graph/device registry; current-state snapshot makes lost transient updates acceptable.

failures.risk: Celebrity/whale user has millions of followers
failures.response: Do not model as ordinary friend fanout; cap product semantics, use pull/cell aggregation, or dedicated topic hierarchy.

questions.q: Why not store every update durably?
questions.a: The product needs current proximity, not an audit trail. Durable high-frequency history is expensive and creates significant privacy risk. Keep only TTL state unless history is an explicit requirement.

questions.q: How do you know which gateway holds a friend?
questions.a: A device registry maps user/device to gateway with TTL and topology epoch. The pub/sub layer may deliver directly to the owning gateway or through a user topic.

questions.q: How do you handle GPS jitter around the radius boundary?
questions.a: Use hysteresis—different enter and leave thresholds—plus minimum dwell time and accuracy radius, so users do not flap in and out.

It can find spatial candidates, but it exposes more users to shared location topics and then requires heavy authorization filtering. For bounded friend graphs, per-user subscriptions are usually safer and cheaper.

mistakes: Persisting precise location indefinitely by default
Broadcasting updates to all users in a cell
Using one fixed update interval regardless of movement/battery
seniorSignal: Treat privacy as a system invariant. Explain soft-state expiry, authorization-before-delivery, adaptive sampling, reconnect semantics, and how you avoid fanout abuse.
implementation: WebSocket gateways with Redis TTL device/location state
Kafka/Redis Streams or a pub/sub fabric partitioned by user ID
Graph cache for friends/blocks and policy versions
Mobile geofencing/motion APIs to reduce update rate
